description: CONDITIONAL_TRUE_EVENT(expr) and CONDITIONAL_CHANGE_EVENT(expr), the two ordered window counters. Both start at 0 per partition. TRUE_EVENT increments on each row up to and including the current one where expr is TRUE - a bare value counts as a boolean, so 0 is falsy, non-zero truthy and NULL not truthy, which is why the bare column and the explicit predicate answer the same sequence. CHANGE_EVENT increments each time expr's value DIFFERS from the previous row's, treating any NULL-involved step as 'not a change', so the trailing NULL carries the previous count rather than raising it. The o_col column {0,0,13,13,14,15,NULL} reproduces the exact sequences the Snowflake docs print: TRUE_EVENT gives 0,0,1,2,3,4,4 and CHANGE_EVENT 0,0,1,1,2,3,3. PARTITION BY resets the count, which the last test shows with a value that DIFFERS across the partition boundary and still restarts at 0. Converted 1:1 from query/WindowConditionalEventTest (now retired); the Java walked the rows keying by seq, so the converted tests pin the whole ordered row set.

steps.sql: CREATE TABLE events (seq INTEGER, o_col INTEGER)
SELECT seq, CONDITIONAL_TRUE_EVENT(o_col) OVER (ORDER BY seq) AS w FROM events ORDER BY seq
CREATE TABLE events (seq INTEGER, o_col INTEGER)
SELECT seq, CONDITIONAL_TRUE_EVENT(o_col > 12) OVER (ORDER BY seq) AS w FROM events ORDER BY seq
CREATE TABLE events (seq INTEGER, o_col INTEGER)
SELECT seq, CONDITIONAL_CHANGE_EVENT(o_col) OVER (ORDER BY seq) AS w FROM events ORDER BY seq
CREATE TABLE readings (province VARCHAR, seq INTEGER, v INTEGER)
SELECT seq, CONDITIONAL_CHANGE_EVENT(v) OVER (PARTITION BY province ORDER BY seq) AS w FROM readings ORDER BY seq
